record.context_brief: Global regularity from smooth initial data
record.original_question: For the three-dimensional incompressible Navier-Stokes equations, starting from a smooth divergence-free initial velocity field, what are the most general assumptions on that initial field that guarantee the existence of a smooth solution for all times t greater than or equal to 0 rather than the formation of a finite-time singularity? The same question is also asked for the Euler equations.

evidence.quote: Question 3.1. What are the most general conditions for smooth initial incompressible velocity field ~v(~x, 0) that ensures that smooth solutions of the Navier-Stokes equations exist for t ≥ 0? The same question holds for Euler’s equations.

Then, question 3.1 is related to the problem of whether the three-dimensional incompressible Navier-Stokes equations can develop a finite time singularity from these smooth initial conditions or if a (unique) global smooth solution exists, which means smooth for all times.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the incompressible Navier–Stokes equations on $\mathbb{R}^3$ (or on the three-dimensional torus $\mathbb{T}^3$):
$$\partial_t v + (v\cdot
abla)v = -
abla p + 
u \Delta v, \qquad 
abla \cdot v = 0,$$
with viscosity $
u > 0$, where $v(x,t)\in\mathbb{R}^3$ is the velocity field and $p(x,t)\in\mathbb{R}$ is the pressure, subject to a smooth, divergence-free initial datum $v(x,0) = v_0(x)$ (with suitable decay at infinity in the $\mathbb{R}^3$ case).

Determine the most general conditions on the smooth divergence-free initial velocity field $v_0$ that ensure the existence (and uniqueness) of a smooth solution $v(\cdot,t)$ for all $t \geq 0$, as opposed to the formation of a finite-time singularity.

Pose the analogous problem for the three-dimensional incompressible Euler equations, obtained by setting $
u = 0$:
$$\partial_t v + (v\cdot
abla)v = -
abla p, \qquad 
abla \cdot v = 0,$$
with smooth divergence-free initial datum $v_0$: identify the most general conditions on $v_0$ that guarantee a globally smooth solution rather than a finite-time blow-up.
artifact.status_search_result: The global regularity problem for the three-dimensional incompressible Navier–Stokes equations remains one of the seven Clay Millennium Prize Problems and is widely considered open. The corresponding global regularity question for the three-dimensional incompressible Euler equations is also open; recent work (e.g., Elgindi 2021, Chen–Hou) has established finite-time singularity formation for certain rough or boundary-data scenarios, but the general smooth-data problem remains unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Navier–Stokes existence and smoothness — Clay Millennium Problem
status_evidence.snippet: The Clay Mathematics Institute lists the Navier–Stokes existence and smoothness problem as one of its unresolved Millennium Prize Problems.
status_evidence.claim: The 3D Navier–Stokes global regularity problem is open.

status_evidence.title: Finite-time singularity formation for C^{1,alpha} solutions to the incompressible Euler equations on R^3
status_evidence.snippet: Elgindi proves finite-time singularity for C^{1,alpha} initial data, but global regularity for smooth data remains open.
status_evidence.claim: The 3D Euler global regularity problem for smooth data remains open.
